title: Minimax Estimation and Honest Inference for the Pointwise CATE Derivative
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4; meets_floor=false; salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: The contribution remains confined to one covariate, exact known uniform design, binary outcomes, and a single fixed smoothness tuple, so it does not provide a general smoothness phase diagram or a random-design frontier.
The KBRW-informed superclass is author-defined and receives only converse transfers, which limits the force of the closest-literature comparison despite the accurate disclosure.

The STEPP discussion supplies motivation but no implementation, numerical illustration, or data analysis, while the enormous deterministic interval constant leaves the practical significance unsupported.

proof_attempt_summary: D0 constructed a same-class lower experiment, a matched n^(-2/13) pointwise CATE derivative risk and honest interval-length frontier, and a fixed-null obstruction compared with an n^(-1/5) known-randomization benchmark. The math and decision reviews passed, but D0.5.G placed the delivered one-dimensional, exact-uniform, fixed-smoothness package at subfield below the field floor. Reaching field tier requires new research on a broader matched frontier or substantive practical demonstration; comparator converse transfers alone do not supply it.
tldr: For the exact-uniform binary class \(\mathcal P_L\), the pointwise CATE derivative has matched minimax absolute-risk and full-class honest connected-interval expected-length rate \(n^{-2/13}\). The fixed-null lower bound holds at the independent fair-coin law, while known randomization admits the faster explicit \(n^{-1/5}\) interval, producing a same-law \(n^{3/65}\) honesty penalty. The exact-uniform class is a strict subclass of an author-defined, KBRW-informed fixed-radius binary comparator class whose indices are source-informed but whose binary sample space, fixed radii, density, overlap, and range restrictions are chosen in this note and are not asserted to equal the published parameter space. Inclusion transfers the risk and fixed-null length converses only to that comparator; the quadratic-moment upper bound and matched frontier remain restricted to \(\mathcal P_L\).
gap: The closest minimax CATE theorem concerns a level target and its lower construction does not preserve an exactly uniform design through nuisance transitions. Existing honest-adaptation theorems concern linear regression functionals, not a nonlinear CATE derivative built from four Bernoulli cells.
fill: The project pairs an observable finite quadratic-moment estimator with a smooth sign-mixture converse whose prior mean is the fixed randomized null, then uses the same testing modulus for minimax risk and fixed-null expected interval length.
